content.title: How powerhouse Michigan outlasted a gritty UConn team to win the 2026 NCAA men's basketball national championship
content.text: Elliot Cadeau scored 19 points as the Wolverines survived the Huskies in a 69-63 rock fightMichigan wins national championship Getty ImagesMichigan defeats UConn to win national championshipThe Michigan Wolverines are the 2026 national champions in men’s college basketball. They have defeated the UConn Huskies 69-63 in a defensive battle at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Elliot Cadeau was the driver of the Michigan offense. The point guard had 19 points on 5-of-11 shooting from the floor.The Wolverines smothered the Huskies, limiting them to 31 percent shooting from the field and 27 percent from 3. UConn also committed 11 turnovers.Michigan has its first NCAA national championship in men’s college basketball since 1989. He and May overlapped at Florida Atlantic University, where Kiffin was the head football coach from 2017-2019 and May was the lead men’s basketball coach from 2018-2024.Mara cuts down the netsYes, even 7-foot-3 Aday Mara needed a ladder in order to cut down the nets during Michigan’s postgame celebration.Way-too-early Top 25 Getty Images Michigan is still celebrating — and will be for quite a while.But while the party rages in Ann Arbor, plenty of other fans are already set to look ahead to the 2026-27 college basketball season.And for those of you who are, we have you covered with CJ Moore’s way-too-early Top 25 featuring a Big Ten team that made plenty of noise in this year’s tournament at No. 1... and Michigan at No. 2.Read on below!SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementDid Michigan's unusual practice strategy pay off? Getty Images This week, as they geared up to play in Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Michigan players went through a shootaround.An outdoor shootaround — in the middle of an empty Michigan Stadium, better known as “The Big House”.The unconventional idea was a brainchild of Dusty May, who wanted his players to get used to shooting in football-sized stadiums.Rustin Dodd has more on May harnessing the power of visualization.Souvenirs from Indianapolis Michael Charles / The AthleticWho needs a t-shirt or a bumper sticker? I’ll take a stat sheet and some confetti!Which cities are next in line to host Final Four? Getty ImagesIndianapolis turned out to be an excellent choice for this year's Final Four. The city was a fitting site for the Big Ten to win its first national title since 2000 given its background as a host of Big Ten championships, and Michigan coach Dusty May reflected back on his roots in the state and with the Hoosiers after winning his first national title.Which cities are set to follow in Indy's footsteps and host future Final Fours?2027: Detroit2028: Las Vegas2029: Indianapolis2030: North Texas/Arlington2031: AtlantaEach of the five sites will use its respective NFL stadium as the arena.Meanwhile in Ann Arbor... Austin Meek / The AthleticThis is the second blazing couch I've already seen tonightReader thoughts on gritty national title game Getty ImagesThe Athletic's readers held a wide range of views on the key stats and impact of the national title game. Here are some additional reader thoughts about Michigan's 69-63 victory:SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMay on what drew him to Michigan Getty ImagesDusty May on the University of Michigan: 💬 “Michigan was a place (where) with a changing landscape, we could retain really good players, even if it wasn’t going great for them. It was going to be hard to leave. .. I just felt like that’s the type of place I would love to coach at.”Lendeborg on return from injury, future Getty ImagesYaxel Lendeborg said he knew he was going to play tonight “as soon as I got back on the court,” adding that “he knew there was no way I was going to miss this game no matter what was going on.”Lendeborg added: 💬 “I was very tentative this game. … I kept having opportunities to make plays and I couldn’t make the play, but these guys stuck with me no matter what they all believed in me. I was trying to push through my mental and physical battle out there dealing with myself but these guys really helped me out and helped me push through.”Lendeborg is still unsure if he’ll need surgery in the offseason, and will find out “in a couple days once we finish celebrating.”The Michigan standout has been open and honest with the pain he’s suffered after enduring an MCL sprain and ankle sprain in the Final Four against Arizona on Saturday. At halftime of the national championship game, Lendeborg told CBS that he feels “awful” and “weak.”Postgame, Lendeborg said he was also dealing with “mental issues.”💬 “These guys all leaned in on me and helped me out, helped me dig myself out of the hole and just continue to keep fighting.”A May masterpiece Getty ImagesDusty May in two seasons at Michigan:64–13 overall record (.831)33-7 in conference play (.825)Winningest season in program history (37-3)2025 Big Ten Tournament champion2026 Big Ten Coach of the Year2026 national championThe Wolverines were 8-24 the season before May joined.May praises Michigan's selflessness Getty ImagesThe two victorious college basketball head coaches, UCLA’s Cori Close and Michigan’s Dusty May, both praised their team’s unselfishness and how “uncommon” — a term both used — this is in college athletics now.May: 💬 “When you bring a group this talented together and they decide from the beginning that they’re going to do it this way and they never waver and they never change, that’s probably the most uncommon thing in athletics now.“For these guys to cut down the nets after all they’ve sacrificed is pretty special.”Michigan a very deserving champion Getty ImagesThe best college basketball team all season won the NCAA Tournament. Doesn't happen all the time, but I like when it does.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementReader thoughts on Michigan's national title Getty ImagesThe Athletic's readers gave Michigan its flowers after a dominant run to a national championship:Among those congratulating Michigan......the United States Department of the Interior, tweeting out a picture of an actual wolverine.Hurley defends instead of criticizing officials Getty ImagesDan Hurley lets out a big laugh when being asked about the officiating, “I know about fines!” and wasn’t outspoken about the officiating, despite appearing frustrated on multiple occasions during the game.💬 “We both played so hard. That’s not an easy game to officiate. If I could have those three guys ref every game the rest of my career, I would sleep well at night.”Hurley loses it when asked about Karaban: 'Changed my life' Getty ImagesOur Lindsay Schnell asked Dan Hurley about Alex Karaban’s impact, and Hurley is all emotions.💬 “Okay, so now the crying.”“This guy changed my life, the staff’s lives, the joy he’s brought to the university, the fan base. … Florida won the National Championship last year. I’ll probably get in trouble for this — Michigan won the national championship this year. But he’s helped to make UConn, I think, right now, we’re probably the premier program in college basketball right now, having been to three out of four National Championship games, having won two of them. He’s put UConn in that rarefied place in college basketball.“Everyone owes everything to that guy.”
